site.title: Local Government Innovation Scan
site.tagline: A daily horizon scan of ideas and technologies reshaping Australian local government.

digests.posture: A quiet mid-week scan with one fresh, in-scope signal — a research/governance signal rather than a marquee pilot. The strongest item is a new QUT report setting out how councils should govern AI as they roll it into statutory and customer-facing work, republished across the sector this week. The hotter frontiers (FOGO/circular economy, AI-assisted development assessment, smart communities) stayed warm but produced no fresh in-window council announcement.

A quiet Monday scan with a single fresh, in-scope signal — an early-stage, climate/circular-economy idea rather than a marquee AI or waste pilot. Shoalhaven's move to repurpose a capped former landfill for a community solar-and-battery hub is the day's one transferable signal, at the awareness/horizon end of the spectrum. The sector's hotter frontiers (FOGO/circular economy, AI-assisted development assessment, smart communities) stayed warm but produced no fresh in-window council announcement.

Quiet Friday scan — no confirmable new, in-scope innovation signal surfaced in the last 24 hours. The sector's active frontiers (FOGO/circular economy, AI-assisted development assessment, AI workforce/governance, smart communities) stay warm but produced no fresh, in-window council announcement today; the strongest in-scope material was either out of window (Moira Shire's resident Emergency Dashboard and Swan Hill's Spendmapp/CityCompass economic-insights tools, both logged 6 August; Port Macquarie-Hastings' mobile licence-plate-recognition parking trial) or ongoing background (the NSW AI Solutions Panel / DAISY development-assessment program; the NSW commercial FOGO source-separation mandate phasing in from 1 July).

A modest Thursday scan with two fresh, in-scope council signals — both from regional Victoria and both about turning data into a resident-facing service. The day's theme is unglamorous but transferable: consolidating live agency feeds and third-party spending data into public dashboards, rather than any marquee AI or circular-economy pilot. The sector's hotter frontiers (FOGO/circular economy, AI-assisted development assessment, smart communities) stayed warm but produced no fresh in-window announcement.

AI moved from single-council experiment toward sector infrastructure today: MAV and ALGA stood up a National AI Working Group while three Adelaide councils jointly bought a four-year AI partner — two different answers to the same question of how a 538-council sector builds AI capability it cannot build alone. Wollongong supplied the day's world-first, and Saturday's watchlist scan produced real yield.

The week's clearest, most transferable innovation signal was the 2026 National Awards for Local Government (announced 23 June) — a deep bench of judged, replicable council projects spanning road safety, sustainable housing, resilient asset rebuilds, libraries and workforce — against a backdrop of active but mostly just-out-of-window waste/circular-economy moves.
